CWU reports stable enrollment with increases in transfer and graduate students
Central Washington University released its Fall 2026 enrollment report showing growth among transfer and graduate students despite an overall flat trend. Retention rates have improved over recent years amid continued sector-wide challenges.
Central Washington University reported on Oct. 14 that its Fall 2026 enrollment figures show several positive trends, according to the annual 10-day census.
The university saw a 4.45% increase in newly enrolled transfer students, rising to 831 from 794 in the previous year. Graduate student enrollment increased by 10.23%, reaching 577 compared to last year's total of 518. The retention rate for full-time, first time in college (FTIC) students improved by 0.9 percentage points, now at 74% compared to last fall's rate of 72.7%.
The FTIC retention rate reflects a notable improvement from earlier years; only 68% of these students returned from fall 2020 to fall 2021. Additionally, the university reported that spring-to-fall re-enrollment remained steady, with about 84% of students who enrolled last spring returning for Fall 2026—the same rate as recorded between spring and fall of the previous year.
CWU President Jim Wohlpart said in an email to campus Tuesday morning, “Seeing our enrollment numbers stabilize — and knowing that we are finding ways to deliver a better educational experience to our students — gives me hope that CWU will meet the many adaptive challenges we are facing and emerge stronger as a result.”
Data from the Office of Institutional Effectiveness, Research, and Planning shows overall enrollment is down slightly by traditional standards: there are currently a total of 8,297 enrolled students compared with last year's figure of 8,334—a difference described as “flat.” The number of FTICs decreased slightly (1,521 this fall versus last year's count of 1,592), as did degree-seeking student numbers (8,104 compared to last year’s total of 8,167).
Wohlpart said in his email that despite ongoing challenges within higher education at both state and national levels since the pandemic began, "CWU has much to celebrate,"
.
